title: POC weekly sync - quantization INT8/FP8
summary: Weekly POC sync to review INT8 vs FP8 quantization experiments. Discussed quality deltas on downstream metrics, perf gains, memory footprint, and next benchmark runs. Agreed to run additional edge-case evals and a 2-week stress run on Dedicated nodes. Planned security doc handoff and pilot pricing check.
topics: memory savings and KV cache behavior
next_steps: Ravi to send trimmed perf microbenchmarks and colab link by 2026-03-19
AcmeAI to provide edge-case prompt set (50 examples) by 2026-03-20
Set up Dedicated 2-week stress run window starting 2026-03-23
Lena to share pilot pricing and security docs (SOC2 summary) by 2026-03-18
action_items: Ravi Patel: produce 4-run perf sheet (INT8/FP8/FP16 baseline) - due 2026-03-19
Tom Rivera: extract 50-edge-case prompts from prod logs - due 2026-03-20
Lena Ortiz: email SOC2 summary + pilot pricing - due 2026-03-18
Nadia Singh: confirm Dedicated window and quota - due 2026-03-19
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 55 minutes on the calendar today. quick roll call?
[00:08] Tom Rivera: tom here, nadia and ethan and olga on our side.
[00:12] Nadia Singh: yep, nadia here.
[00:15] Ravi Patel: ravi from redwood, hi all. maya as well.
[00:18] Ethan Park: ethan, product.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: cool. agenda: quick perf recap, quality deltas on int8 vs fp8, discuss next benchmarks and timeline. ravi, you want to start with numbers?
[01:05] Ravi Patel: sure; so last week we ran the microbench on your 2k token tail workload — baseline fp16, int8 and an fp8 variant. results look like roughly 2.4x throughput improvement int8 vs fp16 on the Dedicated instance type you gave us, and about 1.8x for fp8 depending on kernel. latency P95 dropped from 320ms to 150ms for int8 on short sequences, for long sequences we see caching behaving similar but kernel-switch overhead shows up a bit.
[02:03] Tom Rivera: when you say fp8 gave 1.8x, is that on the same hardware and same batch config?
[02:10] Ravi Patel: same hardware yes; batch config slightly different, we had to tune continuous batching params for fp8 because some kernels prefer smaller micro-batches to avoid dequantization spikes. i'll put the config in the sheet.
[02:35] Olga Petrov: and quality? we care if hallucination rates spike.
[02:38] Ravi Patel: good q. on the standard eval set (the 1k prompt eval you gave) int8 showed a tiny regression ~0.6% on ROUGE-like metric and a 1.1% increase in factuality errors per the automated checker. fp8 was marginally worse on that same set, about 1.3% drop. however on some tasks with numeric precision or tokenization edge cases we saw more pronounced differences.
[03:20] Ethan Park: hmm that 1.1% sounds small but for some customers that could be noticeable. do we have examples?
[03:28] Ravi Patel: yes, olga and team flagged two prompt types — long billing id patterns and code snippets — those had the largest deltas.
[03:40] Olga Petrov: example: a billing id like INV-00001234 sometimes truncated or reformatted in int8 runs. fp8 sometimes inserted an extra dash. it's noisy but reproducible on those patterns.
[03:52] Nadia Singh: that's worrying; our compliance team will flag any change in invoice formatting. we need exact preservation for some flows.
[04:00] Lena Ortiz: understood. that aligns with expected quantization edge cases; we'll propose a hybrid: cache/pin the exact sequence prefixes for those invoice flows and use fp16 for that route, route other traffic to int8. smart routing can help.
[04:20] Tom Rivera: how invasive is that from an infra POV?
[04:24] Maya Chen: not huge — you can set per-route model variants in the Redwood config, pins for prefixes, and automatic fallback to fp16 if the model detects the invoice pattern. the runtime will maintain multiple KV caches but we accounted for that in memory planning.
[05:02] Ravi Patel: memory: int8 saved about 45% memory on host model weights, fp8 saved ~35% relative to fp16 on your hardware. that allowed us to bump batch concurrency which explains throughput gains.
[05:30] Tom Rivera: realistic cost delta if we move to int8?
[05:34] Lena Ortiz: ballpark: on Dedicated the unit token cost comes down ~30-40% factoring infra and licensing assumptions; we'll provide a spreadsheet.
[05:50] Ethan Park: what about KV cache behavior — any regressions to latency when cache hit rates change?
[06:00] Ravi Patel: we saw similar hit rates, but int8 kernel path introduces a tiny dequant step when reusing cached prefix embeddings; on high frequency short requests that adds a small constant ~10ms on cold-cache misses but amortizes out. for heavy streaming load it wasn't material.
[06:40] Olga Petrov: the other thing we care about is eval coverage — our automated factuality checker flagged more false positives when hypotheses changed surface forms. is that the metric you used?
[06:50] Ravi Patel: yes, partly; we also ran an embedding-similarity check and a small human spot check. human check showed some format-preservation issues but not a lot of semantic failures.
[07:10] Tom Rivera: i'd like to see the human examples. can you share the diffs?
[07:13] Ravi Patel: sure, i'll export a diff colab with some samples.
[07:20] Lena Ortiz: next, planned runs: we recommended a 2-week stress run on Dedicated so we can observe production patterns and edge cases. nadia, can you confirm capacity?
[07:30] Nadia Singh: we can allocate a window starting mon 2026-03-23 if that works. need to check quotas but likely yes.
[07:38] Lena Ortiz: perfect.
[08:02] Ravi Patel: also proposal: run targeted edge-case evals — tom/olga to give 50 tricky prompts, we run int8, fp8, fp16, capture diffs and a human label. that will help decide per-route routing.
[08:25] Olga Petrov: we'll pull from prod logs and sanitize.
[08:30] Ethan Park: timeline wise, how soon can we get the perf sheet and the pricing?
[08:34] Lena Ortiz: i'll send pilot pricing and SOC2 summary by end of day 2026-03-18. ravi to send perf microbench by 2026-03-19.
[09:00] Ravi Patel: note on kernels — on your hardware we had to fall back to a slower gemm for fp8 in some layers; there's a kernel-selection tweak we can try next week that might improve fp8 perf ~10% but we need to validate numerics.
[10:10] Tom Rivera: are there any tradeoffs we haven't covered like ephemeral state or cold restart behavior?
[10:18] Maya Chen: cold restarts are similar; int8 model load is smaller so restart is faster but warmup calibration takes a few extra seconds to warm KV caches; nothing catastrophic.
[11:02] Nadia Singh: on security, we need the SOC2 and KMS details. is KMS integrated for Dedicated?
[11:10] Lena Ortiz: yes, KMS/HSM integrations supported; we'll include the summary and entitlements in the doc bundle.
[11:30] Ethan Park: what about monitoring — will regressions trigger alerts?
[11:36] Ravi Patel: we can tie quality monitors to your eval set and trigger regression alerts. Redwood Optimize can suggest fallback thresholds.
[12:00] Tom Rivera: what's the rollback plan if we see production regressions?
[12:05] Maya Chen: automatic fallback to pinned fp16 variants per route, and a canary rollout for any model changes. also we can pin prefix sequences so critical flows never hit quantized variants.
[12:40] Olga Petrov: curious about numerical drift on long dialogs — did you run any multi-turn chat sims?
[12:48] Ravi Patel: we ran a 20-turn sim; int8 had slightly higher token-level instability at turns 12-20 in a small subset, likely due to attention softmax thresholds — we're investigating.
[13:30] Tom Rivera: ok, actionable for us: we'll extract prompt set and confirm Dedicated window.
[13:35] Lena Ortiz: and we'll send perf spreadsheets, diffs, and security bundle. anything else?
[14:02] Ethan Park: one question — competitor note: we heard a vendor offered a custom quant pipeline, want to make sure we address why Redwood's approach is better.
[14:10] Lena Ortiz: our differentiator is runtime + routing + observability — we can do per-route variants and automatic fallbacks, and the Optimize toolkit helps pick quant profiles. will include a short note.
[14:45] Nadia Singh: please include memory forecasts for maintaining multiple KV caches. that's a key ask from infra.
[14:52] Ravi Patel: noted, i'll add memory delta table.
[15:10] Lena Ortiz: ok thanks everyone, wrap up with next steps — recap?
[15:15] Ethan Park: get perf sheets and diffs, edge-case prompts, confirm Dedicated window, pricing+security docs.
[15:30] Lena Ortiz: perfect. we'll follow up via email and slack. meeting adjourned.
notes: Ravi to include kernel-selection notes and config tweaks for fp8
Hybrid routing recommended for invoice flows to preserve exact formatting
